'''Mariann Bienz, Lady Pelham''' (born 21 December 1953, [[Winterthur]]) is a Swiss-British <ref>{{cite web
|title=Mariann Bienz Curriculum Vitae
|url=https://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/groups/bienz/wp-content/uploads/sites/23/Bienz_cvpubl.pdf
|access-date=8 June 2019}}
</ref> [[Molecular biology|molecular biologist]] based at the [[Medical Research Council (UK)|UK Medical Research Council]] [[Laboratory of Molecular Biology]]. She has been a member of their Senior Scientific Staff since 1991,<ref name="AcademyOfMedicalSciences">{{cite web
 |last=Staff 
 |title=The Academy of Medical sciences: Fellows: Dr Mariann Bienz FRS FMedSci 
 |publisher=[[Academy of Medical Sciences]] 
|url=http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/p59fid4730.html 
 |access-date=21 October 2012 
 |url-status=dead 
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110820012208/http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/p59fid4730.html 
 |archive-date=20 August 2011 
}}</ref> was Joint-head of Cell Biology in 2007-08<ref>{{Cite web |last=Biology |first=©2024 MRC Laboratory of Molecular |last2=Avenue |first2=Francis Crick |last3=Campus |first3=Cambridge Biomedical |last4=CB2 0QH |first4=Cambridge |last5=Uk. 01223 267000 |title=Scientific Leadership: Directors, Deputy Directors & Heads of Divisions |url=https://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/about-lmb/scientific-leadership-directors-deputy-directors-heads-of-divisions/ |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology |language=en-GB}}</ref> and has been a Group Leader of Protein and Nucleic Acid Chemistry Division since 2008.<ref>
{{cite web
|title=Protein and Nucleic Acid Chemistry Division
|url=https://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/research/protein-and-nucleic-acid-chemistry/}}
</ref>

==Education==
She was educated at Gymnasium Winterthur and the [[University of Zürich]] where she studied Zoology and Molecular Biology and earned her PhD in 1981.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mariann Bienz Curriculum Vitae|url=https://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/groups/bienz/wp-content/uploads/sites/23/Bienz_cvpubl.pdf|access-date=8 June 2019}}</ref>

Her doctoral thesis, ''Informationelle Suppression bei Drosophila'', was completed in 1981.<ref>{{cite thesis|last=Bienz|first=Mariann|title=Informationelle Suppression bei Drosophila: Entwicklung und Resultate eines «in vivo» Testsystems, basierend auf der Xenopus oocyte|year=1981|url=https://archive.org/details/IA41507219_0023|type=Doctoral thesis|publisher=University of Zürich}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Bienz subsequently undertook [[postdoctoral research]] at the [[Laboratory of Molecular Biology|LMB]] and in 1986 returned to Zürich as assistant professor, and then (1990) associate professor also serving as a member of [[European Molecular Biology Organization|EMBO]] in 1989.<ref name="Debrett's">{{cite web
  | last = Staff
  | title = Dr Mariann Bienz Authorised Biography – Debrett's People of Today, Dr Mariann Bienz Profile
  | publisher = [[Debrett's]]
  | date = 
  | url = http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/browse/b/23181/Mariann+BIENZ.aspx
  | format = 
  | access-date = 21 October 2012}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Married to biologist Sir [[Hugh Pelham]] since 1996.<ref name=ladypelham>{{Who's Who | title=Bienz, Dr Mariann, (Lady Pelham) | id = U44039 | volume = 2015 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
* Member [[European Molecular Biology Organization|EMBO]], 1989<ref name="Bienz2006">{{cite journal|last1=Bienz|first1=M|title=Bio-sketch for Oncogene Review Issue on Wnt signalling|journal=Oncogene|volume=25|issue=57|year=2006|pages=7441|issn=0950-9232|doi=10.1038/sj.onc.1210062|pmid=17143287|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* Friedrich Miescher Prize, Swiss Biochemical Society, 1990
* [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2003|Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS), 2003<ref name=frs>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117112820/https://royalsociety.org/people/mariann-bienz-11083/|archive-date=17 November 2015|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/mariann-bienz-11083/|location=London|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|title=Dr Mariann Bienz FMedSci FRS}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[Academy of Medical Sciences]] (FMedSci), 2006
